subject: Meteorology
title: Cloud Radiative Effects
description: A micro-lesson that makes Cloud Radiative Effects usable.

hook.text: Clouds both cool and warm the Earth—whether they help or hurt depends on their type and altitude.

buildup.text: Low, thick clouds reflect sunlight—cooling the surface. High, thin clouds trap outgoing heat—warming it.

discovery.text: Overall, clouds currently produce a net cooling effect—they reflect more energy than they trap.

twist.text: But as Earth warms, cloud patterns may shift—this 'cloud feedback' is the biggest uncertainty in climate models.

climax.text: Recent evidence suggests warming will reduce low clouds, weakening their cooling—amplifying warming further.

punchline.text: Clouds are climate's wild card—and we're still guessing.

quiz.question: What is the current net effect of clouds on Earth's temperature?
